core_principles.text: Perform the exercise in a standing position with an emphasis on maintaining a controlled and consistent range of motion throughout the entire movement.
Incorporate isometric pauses at 0 degrees, 90 degrees, and 135 degrees of the range of motion to target isometric contractions of the biceps brachii.

specific_findings.text: The study examined ten women subjects with a mean age of 24.4 ± 3.16 years, mean height of 169.4 ± 3.89 cm, and mean weight of 65.3 ± 11.34 kg.
The biceps brachii muscle was modeled with a stiffness of 213 N/m, a dashpot constant of 6.44 Ns/m, and a muscle-tendon length of 0.312 m.
Isometric contractions were evaluated using 5-second pauses at 0 degrees, 90 degrees, and 135 degrees range of motion.

core_principles.text: The highest joint moment and biceps brachii muscle force occur when the elbow joint is fixed at 90 degrees and during movement between 90 and 135 degrees of flexion.
The minimum biceps brachii muscle force occurs during isometric contraction at the largest elbow joint angle of 135 degrees.

common_mistakes.text: Failing to flex the elbow past 90 degrees up to 135 degrees prevents the biceps brachii from experiencing the highest joint moments and muscle forces.

specific_findings.text: In a Finite Element Analysis of ten trained women performing the RPBC exercise, the maximum biceps brachii muscle forces were approximately 200-250 N at 2 kg, 300-350 N at 3 kg, and 450-500 N at 5 kg.
The mean forces generated by the biceps brachii muscle during the RPBC exercise were 169.04 N at 2 kg, 242.63 N at 3 kg, and 362.14 N at 5 kg.
The biceps brachii muscles exhibited maximum displacements of 18.90 µm, 25.76 µm, and 37.56 µm in response to lifting weights of 2 kg, 3 kg, and 5 kg, respectively.
Increasing the dumbbell weight from 2 kg to 3 kg (50% increase) and 3 kg to 5 kg (66.6% increase) resulted in non-linear mean muscle force increases of 43.5% and 49.2%, respectively.

Maximum muscle force was attained at the onset of the t3 movement phase (elbow joint angle increasing from 90 to 135 degrees) and at the onset of the t5 movement phase (elbow joint angle decreasing from 135 to 90 degrees).

core_principles.text: The biceps brachii acts to flex the elbow and supinate the forearm during arm curl exercises.
The Rest-Pause Biceps Curl involves performing a traditional biceps curl with a short rest period between each repetition to allow the muscle to partially recover.

specific_findings.text: In a study of ten women with a mean age of ~24 years, the maximum stress values in the biceps brachii muscle were 180.70 Pa for 2 kg, 246.26 Pa for 3 kg, and 355.89 Pa for 5 kg dumbbells.
The maximum strain values in the biceps brachii muscle were 1.55 x 10^-4 for 2 kg, 2.12 x 10^-4 for 3 kg, and 3.06 x 10^-4 for 5 kg dumbbells.

The mean of the maximum stress-strain values of the subjects increased by ~37% and ~105% relative to the weight ratios of the dumbbells, showing a non-linear correlation between dumbbell weights and stress-strain behavior.
A linear correlation was established between biceps brachii muscle force generation and mechanical behavior changes (stress-strain values) during the exercise.
